recommended_title: Source-Validated Latent-Ability Stacking for Few-Item Benchmark Score Prediction: Small Gains Over Random Subsets and a Persistent Extrapolation Gap
central_question: When only binary per-item results of source models are available and a new model can answer k=100 items, does choosing items by Fisher D-optimal design on a source-fitted logistic latent model and predicting with a source-validated stacked estimator predict full-benchmark accuracy and model ranking better than a random subset mean, k-means anchor points and an IRT-style estimator, especially when the target is stronger than every source model?
central_thesis: On five held-out benchmarks at k=100, the selected stacked latent-model estimator has lower point-estimate MAE than all three trusted baselines (0.0294 vs 0.0339 for the best baseline, a random subset mean) and passed all protocol-validity and negative-control checks, but the paired bootstrap interval for the gain over the best baseline includes zero, and error and rank correlation are about twice as bad for targets stronger than all sources (MAE 0.0409, Spearman 0.730) as for random targets (MAE 0.0179, Spearman 0.956); the evidence supports a modest, statistically unresolved improvement plus a clearly measured extrapolation limitation, not a decisive win.
narrative_rationale: The sealed final evaluation completed with outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome), so the paper may report measured results, but 'qualified' here means protocol validity (all 32 episodes and both negative controls completed, required baselines completed), not superiority; the best-baseline delta CIs span zero (delta MAE CI [-0.0052, 0.0134]; delta utility CI [-0.0143, 0.0354]). The most defensible, reviewer-proof story is therefore a calibrated empirical study: (i) a precisely specified method family (logistic latent model + Fisher D-optimal item design + non-negative stacking validated only on source pseudo-targets with fallback), (ii) honest baselines, (iii) the finding that the dominant failure mode is extrapolation to targets stronger than all sources, which survives a switch from the development benchmarks to five disjoint held-out benchmarks, and (iv) a negative result that bagged posterior-mean and tail calibration add nothing (search utility 0.9445 vs 0.9452). This beats a 'new method wins' framing (not supported by the CI) and beats a chronology of three variants (run-diary). Venue (ICLR, double-blind) rewards calibrated claims, controlled comparisons and explicit scope.

method_groups.name: Source-validated stacked latent estimator (selected configuration, search variant c02)
method_groups.include_reason: Highest search utility (0.9452, 2 seeds) and the frozen choice for the sealed final evaluation (utility 0.9314, 3 seeds, 5 held-out benchmarks). Components: rank-r logistic latent (IRT-style) model fit on source matrix; greedy Fisher D-optimal item selection evaluated at upper-tail reference abilities; target ability by MAP from k answers; linear model-assisted difference estimator and calibrated-mean starter as stack members; non-negative least-squares stacking weights fit only on source pseudo-target folds (strongest-holdout folds for the strong-target regime) with fallback to simpler estimators.

method_groups.name: Linear model-assisted D-optimal estimator (search variant c01)
method_groups.include_reason: Earlier, simpler configuration (search utility 0.9381) that the stack contains as a fallback member; serves as a within-family reference showing what logistic modelling/Fisher design/stacking added, with the caveat that it is a cumulative-change comparison on 2 search seeds, not a clean single-factor ablation.

method_groups.name: Bagged posterior-mean + tail-calibration extension (search variant c03)
method_groups.include_reason: Negative result: added a fourth stack candidate for strong targets but did not improve over the stack (0.9445 vs 0.9452; MAE strong 0.0362 vs 0.0359; Spearman strong 0.812 vs 0.816). Reported briefly as evidence that further tail correction on source pseudo-targets did not help.

method_groups.name: Trusted baselines: random subset mean, k-means anchor points, IRT-style estimator
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned matched comparators at the same k=100 on the same episodes; random subset mean is the best baseline by utility (delta vs best baseline equals delta vs random mean). Final-evaluation MAE improvements: 0.0045 vs random mean, 0.0134 vs anchor points, 0.0398 vs IRT-style (positive = candidate better; CI available only for the best-baseline/random-mean comparison).

method_groups.name: Negative controls (permuted targets, constant targets)
method_groups.include_reason: Show that predictions depend on the target's revealed answers (permuted-targets Spearman drop 1.157, MAE increase 0.156; constant-targets MAE delta 0.094 in final) so the reported accuracy is not a protocol artifact.

results_focus: Held-out final comparison (5 disjoint benchmarks, 3 seeds, k=100): candidate MAE 0.0294, RMSE 0.0354, Spearman 0.843, Kendall 0.715, utility 0.9314 versus baselines; MAE deltas +0.0045 (random mean), +0.0134 (anchor points), +0.0398 (IRT-style); paired hierarchical bootstrap (benchmarks, seeds, target models; 300 replicates, 95% percentile interval) for the best-baseline gap: MAE [-0.0052, 0.0134], utility [-0.0143, 0.0354] -- both include zero, so state 'improvement not statistically resolved'.

Regime breakdown on the final evaluation: random targets MAE 0.0179 / Spearman 0.956 versus strong targets (stronger than every source; sources are below the 0.7 quantile of model score) MAE 0.0409 / Spearman 0.730; same pattern on search benchmarks for all three variants (strong-target MAE roughly 2x random-target MAE). Per-regime baseline numbers are not in the artifacts: do not claim where the gain over baselines is concentrated.
Negative-control sanity checks (final): permuted and constant targets degrade the prediction as expected.

Within-family variant comparison on search benchmarks (2 seeds, all 3 of 3 variants scored, 0 unscored): utility 0.9381 -> 0.9452 -> 0.9445; strong-target Spearman 0.771 -> 0.816 -> 0.812; difference between the two top variants (0.0006) is smaller than the seed-to-seed spread within a variant (e.g. 0.9423 vs 0.9480), so the choice of c02 over c03 is not statistically supported; c01->c02 gain (+0.0071) is larger but still from 2 seeds.

Search-to-final shift: utility 0.9452 (search, 5 development benchmarks, 2 seeds) vs 0.9314 (final, 5 disjoint benchmarks, 3 seeds); do not attribute the drop to a cause (different benchmarks and seeds); report as measured and keep search and final in separate tables/panels.
Scope statement: single budget k=100, binary accuracy only, one target-regime definition, 5+5 benchmarks; no sweep over k, no ablations beyond the three variants.
figure_plan: Fig. 1 (overview, page 1-2): prediction protocol and method at a glance -- source binary matrix -> logistic latent fit -> Fisher D-optimal selection of k=100 items -> target answers on selected items -> stacked estimator with source pseudo-target validation and fallback -> predicted full accuracy; side inset contrasting the two target regimes (random vs stronger than all sources).

Fig. 2 (main result, held-out final benchmarks): panel A overall MAE of candidate vs random subset mean, anchor points, IRT-style (baseline MAE obtained as candidate MAE + reported delta, labelled derived); panel B paired improvement vs the best baseline (MAE and utility) with 95% bootstrap intervals that visibly cross zero.
Fig. 3 (extrapolation gap): MAE and Spearman for random vs strong targets, shown for development (search) and held-out (final) benchmark groups in separate, clearly labelled categories.

Table 1: final-evaluation metrics (MAE, RMSE, Spearman, Kendall, utility), per-seed utility (0.9257, 0.9324, 0.9360), controls. Table 2: search-stage variant comparison with per-seed utilities and strong/random breakdown.

planned_subsections.heading: Evaluation protocol and metric definitions
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Episode structure (source matrix only, <=100 items, target answers on selected items only), random vs strong target construction (20% of models as targets; strong targets drawn from models at or above the 0.7 quantile of accuracy with sources strictly below it; minimum 40 sources), utility definition 0.5*clip(1-2*MAE,0,1)+0.5*(Spearman+1)/2, aggregation (seeds -> benchmarks -> 0.5/0.5 regimes), bootstrap procedure, benchmark names for development (ifeval, arc_challenge, musr, gsm, bbh) and held-out (gpqa, med_qa, legalbench, mmlu, mmlu_pro) groups.

planned_subsections.heading: Estimator and stacking details of the selected configuration
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Rank grid, Newton/IRLS fitting, Gaussian-prior MAP ability, Fisher D-optimal greedy design at upper-tail reference abilities, NNLS stacking weights over source pseudo-target folds, fallback logic; hyperparameters taken from the program source for the selected search variant.

planned_subsections.heading: Search-stage variant results
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Full metric table for the three scored variants (utility, MAE, RMSE, Spearman, Kendall, per-regime MAE/Spearman, deltas vs baselines, per-seed utilities 0.9369/0.9393, 0.9423/0.9480, 0.9423/0.9468), plus a statement that all 3 of 3 variants were scored and none unscored.

planned_subsections.grounded_content: All final metrics with per-seed utilities (0.9257, 0.9324, 0.9360), baseline deltas, both bootstrap intervals (MAE and utility), control metrics, number of episodes (32 completed, 0 failed) and RPC calls (128).

notes_for_writer: Use reader-facing names: 'utility score' (define it explicitly) instead of the internal combined score; 'model variants', 'seeded runs', 'configurations'. Never show internal field names.

Final facts must cite final.* sources; search facts cite result.* sources. Keep search (development benchmarks, seeds 11/12) and final (held-out benchmarks, seeds 9101-9103) numbers in separate tables/panels and never pool them.

Qualification: final.qualification.outcome is 'qualified', status 'completed', correct True. Say explicitly that in this task 'qualified' denotes protocol validity (all episodes, controls and baselines completed); it is not a superiority or generalization claim. candidate_diagnostics_trust is 'unverified' in the evidence files; mention this limitation. No gate-level diagnostics are provided for why any criterion would fail, so make no cause attribution of that kind.

Sign convention (from the evaluator source): delta_mae = baseline MAE - candidate MAE and delta_score = candidate utility - baseline utility, so positive favours the candidate. State this once. The best baseline by utility is the random subset mean (best-baseline and random-mean deltas are identical).

Bootstrap intervals (95% percentile, 300 replicates; resampling benchmarks, then seeds, then target models) include zero for the best-baseline gap on both MAE and utility; phrase as 'point-estimate improvement not statistically resolved'. No CI is available for the anchor-points and IRT-style deltas, so do not call those significant either; but the anchor and IRT-style deltas are larger in point estimate. No per-regime baseline numbers exist: do not state that the method helps more for random or strong targets than baselines do.

Baseline MAEs shown in figures are derived (candidate MAE + reported delta): random mean 0.0339, anchor points 0.0428, IRT-style 0.0692; label them 'derived from reported deltas'. Baseline Spearman values are not available; do not plot them.

Variant comparison is a cumulative-change comparison on 2 search seeds; there is no single-factor ablation (ablation_studies is empty). Do not attribute the c01->c02 gain to a specific component (logistic model vs Fisher design vs stacking) and do not describe c03 as hurting; it is statistically indistinguishable. The top-two gap (0.0006) is below within-variant seed spread, so present selection of c02 as the frozen choice, not as a demonstrated best.

Planned analyses in the idea files (k sweep over 20-200, 20+ seeds, MMLU-Pro/BBH emphasis, latent-rank and shrinkage ablations, temporal split) were NOT run; the evaluator uses only k=100. Do not claim them; list the k sweep and ablations as untested in the limitations.
The drop from search utility 0.9452 to final 0.9314 occurs across disjoint benchmarks and different seeds; report it without a causal explanation.
